QF.id: AIFM CIII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_30

question.text: If a Cat III AIF scheme FAILS to obtain 75% investor consent for in-specie distribution during the Liquidation Period, the unliquidated investments shall be:

answer.text: Continued to be held until liquidity emerges
Distributed mandatorily in-specie at One Rupee for performance-benchmarking purposes
Forcibly sold at any market-clearing price by SEBI
Transferred to a Cat II AIF for continued management

explanation.text: The Logic: Where the requisite 75% investor consent for in-specie distribution is not obtained, the unliquidated investments are mandatorily distributed in-specie at a value of One Rupee. This value is what is captured in the manager's track record and reported to the Performance Benchmarking Agency. An investor unwilling to accept the Re. 1 valuation must write off the investment. The Trap: Option A ignores the mandatory distribution trigger. Options C and D invent powers or routes (SEBI-directed forced sale, transfer to a Cat II AIF) that the workbook does not provide. Note: The Re. 1 mandatory in-specie distribution rule appears in the workbook on pp. 358-359. It is the default consequence of failing the 75% consent vote during the Liquidation Period.
